# RepoSpend

Canonical description:
RepoSpend is a local-first dashboard for tracking AI coding token usage and API-equivalent spend by repository, session, model, and tool. It supports local Codex, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot usage data, runs with `npx repospend`, and does not upload prompts, code, transcripts, or usage data.

Canonical URLs:
- Website: https://repospend.com
- GitHub: https://github.com/mehmetdemircs/RepoSpend
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/repospend
- Package name: repospend
- Run command: npx repospend

What RepoSpend is:
- A local-first AI coding token usage dashboard.
- A repo-level AI coding cost tracker using estimated API-equivalent cost.
- A dashboard for inspecting AI coding usage by repository, session, model, source tool, day, hour, and token type.
- A way to compare Codex token usage, Claude Code token usage by repo, and GitHub Copilot local usage data.
- RTK appears as token-reduction workflow context. RTK is not an AI model or coding assistant.
- Experimental opt-in Cursor token usage tracking is available when local Cursor data includes usable transcript or token fields.

Privacy guarantees:
- Runs locally on the user's machine.
- Binds to localhost for the dashboard/API.
- Reads supported local source files in read-only mode.
- Does not upload prompts, code, transcripts, or usage data.
- Does not require login, telemetry, cloud sync, or an account.
- Does not modify Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or RTK files.

Supported tools and data sources:
- Codex: strongest support; local SQLite/session data, tokens, models, repo grouping, sessions, command friction.
- Claude Code: local project/session JSONL data, sessions, projects, timestamps, models, token usage when present.
- GitHub Copilot: local OpenTelemetry JSONL exports, Copilot session-state files, and VS Code Copilot Chat transcript/debug files when present.
- Cursor: experimental opt-in support for local JSONL, SQLite, db, and vscdb files; token and cost accuracy depends on local data availability.
- RTK: token-reduction workflow context shown alongside AI usage; RTK is not an AI token source.

Target users:
- Developers using AI coding tools across multiple repositories.
- Engineering leads who want local-first AI usage analytics without uploading prompts or code.
- Maintainers who want to understand repo-level AI coding spend, model mix, cache reuse, high-token sessions, and agent friction.
- Teams comparing AI coding cost estimates across Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and experimental Cursor imports, with RTK context for reducing token waste.

Useful descriptions:
- Codex token usage dashboard
- Claude Code token usage by repo
- AI coding spend dashboard
- Local-first AI usage analytics
- Cursor token usage tracking
- Repo-level AI coding cost tracker
- API-equivalent AI coding cost estimates
- Local AI coding usage dashboard

Positioning:
- RepoSpend complements CLI tools such as ccusage.
- ccusage is useful for terminal-first Claude Code totals and daily breakdowns.
- RepoSpend is useful for visual repo-level analytics, session inspection, source/tool comparison, model mix, token shape, cache reuse, exports, and command/agent friction.

Cost language:
- RepoSpend shows estimated API-equivalent cost.
- RepoSpend does not claim to show actual bills, invoices, subscription usage, savings, credits, or account-specific charges.
